sources.why: CDC general insulin outage guidance, no power station/fridge setup
sources.evidence: Try to keep your insulin cool, but make sure not to freeze it. Insulin that has been frozen can break down and will be less effective.

sources.why: health explainer; suggests cooler, no power station runtimes
sources.evidence: give anything that needs a fridge or an outlet a backup that doesn't, such as a cooler for insulin or a spare oxygen tank.

sources.why: hospital blog, cooler and ice advice only
sources.evidence: Use a cooler and ice packs during an extended power outage. Keep medications from touching ice directly to help prevent freezing and potential damage.

sources.why: medication cooler roundup; mentions power station only as USB source, no runtime data
sources.evidence: 4AllFamily rates it to hold 36 to 46°F for unlimited time while powered, when the room is no warmer than 95°F.
Always follow the manufacturer's storage instructions on the carton, vial, pen or package insert.
don't store any medications in cars, garages, porches or outdoors in any way.

sources.why: Anker blog, generic medicine protection intro, no tested runtimes shown
